name: Thought Leaders Issue 1: AI — African Reality vs African Fiction
description: Africa wants AI. The question is who owns the layer it runs on. Africa holds less than 1% of the world's data-centre capacity, and much of the continent's AI is built on models trained elsewhere and reached through services that can be withdrawn, repriced or restricted from another country. This mini-book separates the fiction from the reality: South Africa's GPU "AI factory", Nigeria's N-ATLaS language model, Kenya's stalled Olkaria data centre, Ethiopia's AI policy and institute, Zimbabwe's data-sovereignty strategy, Burkina Faso's new AI roadmap and Mali's Bambara school books made with AI. Inside this 15-page A5 mini-book: • Where Africa's compute actually lives, with an illustrated map of the AI stack • Why a mobile-first economy finds the AI race hard to run • Building on borrowed foundation models, and the African teams building their own • Four countries the headlines skip: Ethiopia, Zimbabwe, Burkina Faso and Mali • The off switch: what remote frontier AI means for sovereignty • Five key actions (opportunity, action, valuable outcome) for students, business executives, lobbyists, software builders and communities, each with resources you can use today • An AI readiness table covering all 54 African countries Every factual claim is referenced to a live public source (36 references). Price: £3.60 per issue, including VAT. More from the series: www.africavsthefuture.xyz Part of the Africa vs The Future Thought Leaders Series: short, referenced, actionable.
